name: Mike Malott
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: Canada's leading welterweight (14-2-1, 7-1 UFC) on a four-fight win streak, most recently a third-round TKO of Gilbert Burns in his first UFC main event in April. A long, technical kickboxer with a real submission game; his one UFC loss came when he faded and was stopped late by Neil Magny.

how_they_fight.Striking: Accurate (about 50%) and varied: jab, leg and body kicks, and clean uppercut/hook combinations in the pocket. Against Burns (per Sherdog's play-by-play) he walked him to the fence, hurt him with an uppercut in round two, and dropped him twice in round three (uppercut and left hook, then a right hand) for the TKO at 2:08. Two knockdowns against Burns and one each against Mickey Gall and Charles Radtke.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Dangerous front-headlock and back-take submission game: six career submissions (five in round one), including Yohan Lainesse (R1) and Adam Fugitt (R2) in the UFC. Wrestles mostly defensively; he stuffed every Burns shot and won 362 seconds of control on Magny before fading.
how_they_fight.Defense: Stuffs takedowns well when fresh (Burns went 0-for-7 per our data). Stopped twice: Hakeem Dawodu (KO R1, 2014) and Neil Magny (TKO R3 at 4:45, January 2024), when he was clearly ahead but tired. Burns hurt his lead leg with calf kicks and a kick dropped him to a knee in round two.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Historically a fast starter: 9 of his 12 stoppage wins came in round one. Recent fights have gone longer: decisions over Trevin Giles and Kevin Holland and the R3 Burns finish. The worry is the Magny fight, where he was described as gassed in round three and stopped with 15 seconds left. He has never fought past round three; this is his second five-round booking and the first time he may see round four.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Composed and disciplined at range; manages distance and picks shots instead of brawling. The Holland win was marred by two accidental low blows in round one (no point deducted), and he took over once Holland was compromised.

patterns: Early finisher: 9 of 12 stoppage wins in round 1 (overall); UFC finishes in R1 (Gall, Lainesse), R2 (Fugitt, Radtke) and R3 (Burns)
Pins opponents on the fence and lands uppercuts and hooks in the pocket
Strong takedown defense when fresh; sprawls and counters
Goes to the front headlock / back for submissions when opponents shoot or are hurt
Has never been past round 3; the only late stoppage loss came when he tired (Magny, R3)
concerns: Cardio over five rounds is unproven; faded badly late against Magny
Lead leg can be attacked: Burns's calf kicks dropped him to a knee
Age (mid-30s) and the pressure of headlining at home again
keys_to_beat: Survive and slow him early, then push the pace into rounds 3-5
Attack the lead leg with calf kicks
Wrestle late when he tires, as Magny did
Don't shoot sloppy entries into his front headlock

news.text: Headlines UFC Edmonton against Joaquin Buckley, his sixth straight fight in Canada (per UFC.com) and second UFC main event.
Betting favourite at -140 against Buckley (+120), per MMA Junkie.
Stopped Gilbert Burns in round 3 in Winnipeg for a Performance of the Night bonus; Burns retired afterwards.
